svg.title: Stable images before the cache boundary, volatile ones after it
svg.desc: A hand-drawn prompt bar divided into segments: system prompt and tools, both stable; a reference image stable across the session; then a dashed cache boundary; then a live screenshot that is new every turn, and the user turn. Notes explain that anything before the boundary — a reference document or fixed diagram — is an excellent caching candidate, paying the write premium once and reading back at about a tenth of input price, while a live screenshot changes every turn and placed early would break the prefix and send every earlier token back to full price. Three cards below give the screenshot-stream disciplines: downscale aggressively since a click target needs no pixel-perfect detail, prune old screenshots and summarise them as text, and annotate what was done rather than re-sending pixels. Captions note there is no separate image budget and that a long strip of screenshots suffers the same lost-in-the-middle problem as long text.
svg.text: Where an image sits decides whether it caches
Caching keys on an exact prefix match. A picture that changes every turn cannot be part of one.
A reference document or a fixed diagram, stable across many turns, is an
excellent caching candidate: pay the write premium once, read it back at about
a tenth of input price for the rest of the session.
A live screenshot changes every turn, so it can never be cached.
Placed early it would break the prefix and send every earlier token
Send the smallest screenshot the model can
still read. A click target does not need
Keep the most recent few. Summarise the
Once the model has read a screen and
acted, a short note of what it did is far
There is no separate image budget. 30k tokens of text plus 20k of images is a 50k-token prompt, for the window, the price, and the prefill.
A long strip of screenshots suffers the same lost-in-the-middle problem as long text: the middle turns get the least attention.
